Visa, Stripe, Mastercard, BlackRock, and Coinbase are launching a new stablecoin, OUSD

The largest financial and crypto companies have announced the launch of the Open Standard (OUSD) stablecoin. The project involves Visa, Stripe, Mastercard, BlackRock, Coinbase, as well as several dozen other companies.


Partners of the project will receive all profits from the reserves of the stablecoin, deducting a small fee for Open Standard's operational expenses. This differs from most existing stablecoins where the issuer (Tether or Circle) keeps the majority of the profit for themselves.

OUSD is positioned as an open standard, in which several major players act as both issuers and beneficiaries simultaneously. This is intended to increase trust in the stablecoin among institutional investors and traditional financial companies.

- Create an alternative to USDT and USDC with a more distributed revenue model.
- Simplify the integration of stablecoins for large companies (Visa, Mastercard, Stripe).
- Attract institutional capital through the participation of BlackRock and other traditional players.
- Reduce the concentration risks present in centralized stablecoins.

Official details about the backing of OUSD (which assets will be in reserves) and the exact mechanics of profit distribution among participants have not been disclosed yet. It is expected that more detailed information will be available in the coming weeks.

The project is already being hailed as one of the most serious attempts by the traditional financial world to create its own major stablecoin.

📌 Perpetual Futures (Perps): Trading Without Expiry Dates

Main Points
⏺ Perpetual futures let you long or short crypto with leverage and no expiration
⏺ A funding rate keeps perp prices close to the spot market
⏺ This post explains how perps work and why they dominate crypto derivatives

1️⃣ Basic Idea — perps are contracts that track an asset’s price, letting you bet up or down without owning the coin
2️⃣ No Expiry — unlike traditional futures, perps don’t settle on a fixed date, so you can hold as long as your margin allows
3️⃣ Funding Rate — periodic payments flow between longs and shorts to keep perp prices aligned with spot
4️⃣ Leverage — exchanges let you control large positions with relatively small capital, amplifying both gains and losses
5️⃣ Who Uses Them — traders hedge positions, speculate on moves, or build structured strategies using perps as core tools

Final Thoughts

Perpetual futures give traders flexible exposure to crypto markets — powerful tools, but unforgiving if you don’t manage risk.

Binance has warned its European users that it will stop providing crypto services in the EU after failing to secure a MiCA license before the deadline

On June 24, the exchange withdrew its license application in Greece and announced plans to apply in another EU country. However, with MiCA rules fully taking effect on July 1, time has run out. 

In emails sent to users, Binance's European entity stated that it can no longer accept new clients and will cease providing crypto-asset services from July 1, 2026.

Users in Poland, Italy, Spain, and France have already received instructions on how to withdraw their funds. 

Binance founder Changpeng Zhao criticized the decision, saying it's "sad to see the European Union deprive its users of access to the best liquidity in the world."

For now, this looks like a major setback for Binance in Europe and another reminder that regulation is becoming one of the biggest challenges for global crypto exchanges.

🤖 How an MEV bot quietly robs you on an EVM DEX — and why it can't on GalaSwap

Every time you swap on Uniswap, PancakeSwap, or any EVM DEX, you're not just trading against the pool. You're trading in front of an audience of predatory bots. Here's exactly how they skim your trade, step by step:

1️⃣ You broadcast your swap. It doesn't execute instantly — it lands in the public mempool, a glass waiting room where every pending transaction is visible to anyone watching. That includes hundreds of MEV bots scanning in real time.

2️⃣ A searcher spots you. It calculates: "jump in front, move the price against them, dump right after for a guaranteed profit." It fires two transactions — one before you, one after — and bids higher gas to lock in that ordering.

3️⃣ You get sandwiched. The bot buys *first* (price ↑), your order fills at the worse price, and it sells *immediately after* into the demand you created. You paid more. It pocketed the difference.

Good morning from the North Pacific Ocean as we make our way from Seattle to Alaska.

I woke up at 2:00 a.m. with a heart full of gratitude - for my family and for the wonderful people who have joined us for this conference aboard this magnificent ship. By 3:30 a.m., I found myself working out in the ship’s gym, where I often reflect on the times in which we live and the direction our world is heading. This morning was no different.

I am also deeply thankful for this remarkable group of speakers, each of whom I regard as an outstanding teacher of God’s Word and a living reflection of His character.

Truthfully, with speakers of this caliber, I would much rather sit, listen, and learn than stand and teach.

A day at sea is also a day of reflection.

For me, as many of you know, in light of recent events, the heaviness and sadness I carry on this semiquincentennial birthday of America are even greater. In 1948, there were great Americans who understood the magnitude of that historic moment and did everything they could to help the newborn - and only - Jewish state.

Even the legendary Frank Sinatra played his part. Evading federal agents in 1948, he reportedly slipped out the back of a New York nightclub carrying a paper bag filled with one million dollars in cash to pay a ship captain for a critical, embargo-breaking shipment of munitions destined for Israel.

At the time, the United States had imposed a general arms embargo on the Middle East. Although it officially applied to all parties, it left the newly established State of Israel desperately short of weapons while neighboring Arab armies were already well-equipped through other sources. Yet the Lord always raised up men and women who understood the significance of the hour and gave them the courage to act upon their convictions.

Even now, as we face rising hostility toward Israel, it is worth reflecting on how extraordinary this relationship truly is. Here are two nations with no shared border, no meaningful economic dependence, and not even a common language - yet for decades they have been uniquely connected. No obvious national self-interest brought them together in the beginning. Rather, something deep within the American spirit has long been drawn to the story of the Jewish people and their return to their ancestral homeland.

And here I am, aboard an American cruise ship, sailing toward God’s breathtaking creation in Alaska - not only to behold His magnificent handiwork, but also surrounded by nearly 700 like-minded believers who understand the significance of the times and seasons in which we live.

Even if political leaders change course, pursue profit from the wrong places, or make deals with the worst of America’s enemies, the saints gathered here understand that in these last days courage is a rare commodity - one that God expects, requires, and calls His people to demonstrate.

At times, standing for the truth may make us feel as though we are standing alone. Elijah felt exactly that way. Yet the Lord gently corrected his perception, reminding him that He had preserved a faithful remnant of 7,000 in Israel who had not bowed the knee to Baal (1 Kings 19:18). The same God who preserved a remnant then is preserving one today.

God has never needed the majority to accomplish His purposes. He has always worked through a faithful remnant. Our calling is not to be popular, but to be faithful - to speak the truth in love (Ephesians 4:15), contend earnestly for the faith (Jude 3), and leave the results to Him.

Hours, days, and even years of advocating for Israel ultimately mean very little if they are detached from the Word of God, the plan of God, and the love of God displayed through our precious Messiah, Yeshua. Israel matters because God says it matters. Our convictions must always be rooted in Scripture, never merely in politics or emotion.

I cannot wait to share, toward the end of this cruise, my new message, “Certainly Not!” - God’s answer to the doubts, distortions, and false teachings surrounding His plans and purposes for Israel.

The TRUMP Rally vs. the American Dream

Trump turned the 250th anniversary into a branded spectacle — “the most spectacular TRUMP RALLY of them all” — and forced Democrats into the least glamorous job in American politics: explaining patriotism while he sells it like merch.

In Washington, patriotism now looks like tanks, flyovers, fireworks and a giant fair on the National Mall patrolled by National Guard troops, with the president literally on the marquee. 

Anyone who skips it risks looking anti‑American by definition. Trump ties love of country to loyalty to himself, then dares Democrats to say no.

Wes Moore, Josh Shapiro, Rosie Rios and a crop of candidates like Rebecca Bennett are busy building a parallel Fourth of July: museum exhibits, naturalization ceremonies, community service projects, state‑house speeches in Annapolis instead of on the Mall. 

Moore explicitly says it’s time to “stop ceding the flag,” while Shapiro calls Trump’s version “whitewashing history” and stripping rights. Bennett talks about patriotism as ROTC, the GI Bill, a VA loan — not a stadium chant.

They’re all trying to hack the definition. One camp pushes “patriotism = defending democracy from Trump’s agenda.” Another leans into reckoning with slavery and inequality. A third sells patriotism as economic security and a shot at the American Dream, because voters now say they feel more betrayed by broken finances than by whether someone wears a flag pin. 

Only 18 percent of Americans see Democrats as “very patriotic,” versus 31 percent for Republicans. You don’t flip that with one speech.

Republicans, predictably, play the same old card with a new face. Nixon did it in Vietnam, Reagan in the Cold War, Bush Sr. with flag‑waving in 1988. Now Trump wraps the entire semiquincentennial in his own persona and accuses critics of hating the country, not him. 

GOP operatives sneer that Democrats would be “beating their chest” about unity if Kamala Harris were president, and that boycotting the Mall fair is just taking their ball and going home.

Underneath the noise, something more basic is breaking. For decades, the fight was over symbols: flags, anthems, pins. Now, polarization means accusations of corruption, authoritarianism or historical denial bounce off because each side hears only that “their guy” is under attack. 

Trump is explicit about it: “I found out that nobody cared.” If nobody cares, then the guardrails that used to separate patriotism from personality cult become just another trench in the same culture war.

Democrats are trying to sell a version of patriotism that doesn’t require saluting Trump’s stage — rights, institutions, service, a country that can be loved and criticized at the same time. Trump is trying to sell one that does. On the 250th anniversary, the flag hasn’t changed. The ownership claim has.
